comment:
* A policy on how much time to spend on a task before giving up. When a task * times out, it is left in an unspecified state and should be abandoned. For * example, if reading from a source times out, that source should be closed and * the read should be retried later. If writing to a sink times out, the same * rules apply: close the sink and retry later. * *

Timeouts and Deadlines

* This class offers two complementary controls to define a timeout policy. * *

Timeouts specify the maximum time to wait for a single * operation to complete. Timeouts are typically used to detect problems like * network partitions. For example, if a remote peer doesn't return any * data for ten seconds, we may assume that the peer is unavailable. * *

Deadlines specify the maximum time to spend on a job, * composed of one or more operations. Use deadlines to set an upper bound on * the time invested on a job. For example, a battery-conscious app may limit * how much time it spends preloading content. * @hide This class is not part of the Android public SDK API

variables.name: NONE
variables.comment:
* An empty timeout that neither tracks nor detects timeouts. Use this when
   * timeouts aren't necessary, such as in implementations whose operations
   * do not block.

variables.name: hasDeadline
variables.comment:
* True if {@code deadlineNanoTime} is defined. There is no equivalent to null
   * or 0 for {@link System#nanoTime}.

methods.name: public Timeout timeout(long timeout, TimeUnit unit)
methods.comment:
* Wait at most {@code timeout} time before aborting an operation. Using a * per-operation timeout means that as long as forward progress is being made, * no sequence of operations will fail. * *

If {@code timeout == 0}, operations will run indefinitely. (Operating * system timeouts may still apply.)

methods.name: public long timeoutNanos()
methods.comment: Returns the timeout in nanoseconds, or {@code 0} for no timeout.

methods.name: public boolean hasDeadline()
methods.comment: Returns true if a deadline is enabled.

methods.name: public long deadlineNanoTime()
methods.comment:
* Returns the {@linkplain System#nanoTime() nano time} when the deadline will
   * be reached.
   *
   * @throws IllegalStateException if no deadline is set.

methods.name: public Timeout deadlineNanoTime(long deadlineNanoTime)
methods.comment:
* Sets the {@linkplain System#nanoTime() nano time} when the deadline will be
   * reached. All operations must complete before this time. Use a deadline to
   * set a maximum bound on the time spent on a sequence of operations.

methods.name: public final Timeout deadline(long duration, TimeUnit unit)
methods.comment: Set a deadline of now plus {@code duration} time.

methods.name: public Timeout clearTimeout()
methods.comment: Clears the timeout. Operating system timeouts may still apply.

methods.name: public void throwIfReached() throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Throws an {@link InterruptedIOException} if the deadline has been reached or if the current
   * thread has been interrupted. This method doesn't detect timeouts; that should be implemented to
   * asynchronously abort an in-progress operation.

methodNames: public Timeout timeout(long timeout, TimeUnit unit)
public final Timeout deadline(long duration, TimeUnit unit)
